title: SchedulerProblem
description: One tick of work handed to the airtime solver. The control plane owns RF prediction and demand estimation; the solver owns nothing but the allocation decision, so it stays pure and testable.

epoch.description: Monotonic tick counter. The control plane rejects a plan whose epoch does not match the problem it sent, which is how a slow solver run gets discarded instead of applied late.

tick_seconds.description: Seconds this allocation is expected to hold. Starlink reassigns terminals on 15s boundaries; fixed towers can safely use longer.

handoff_gain_threshold.description: A terminal only moves when the new sector scores this multiple of its current one. 1.0 means move on any improvement, which produces flapping. 1.2 to 1.4 is sane.

min_dwell_seconds.description: A terminal that has just moved is pinned for this long, even if something better appears. The second half of flap protection.

stickiness.description: Score bonus applied to a terminal's current sector, as a fraction. Expresses that a working link has value beyond its bitrate.

reserve_committed_first.description: Reserve every terminal's committed rate before distributing surplus. Turning this off makes the network faster on average and breaks the only promise you actually sold.

parent_site_id.description: Empty when the site reaches the PoP directly. Otherwise this site's traffic is also charged against the parent's backhaul, recursively.

backhaul_sector_id.description: Set when this site relays over a parent sector's air interface rather than its own circuit. The relay then competes for airtime with that sector's subscribers.

airtime_budget.description: Schedulable fraction of a second, after management overhead and a deliberate latency reserve.

priority.description: Plan priority. Higher wins scarce airtime. Used as the weight in weighted max-min fairness.

demand_down_mbps.description: Estimated offered load, not the plan ceiling. Allocating to ceilings wastes the whole network, since subscribers are idle most of the time.

current_sector_id.description: Empty for a terminal that is not yet associated.

dwell_seconds.description: How long the terminal has held its current sector.

pinned_sector_id.description: Operator override. Honoured unconditionally; the solver reports when the pin costs the subscriber their committed rate rather than silently overriding it.

candidates.description: Every sector this terminal could use, with the rate each would deliver. An empty list means the terminal is unserviceable this tick, which is an answer, not an error.

measured.description: True when sinr_db came from the terminal's own report rather than the propagation model. Measured values are trusted over predictions, and the gap between them is how the model gets calibrated.
